deck_invariants.frontier: Reconstruction is already verified by computer through at least 11 vertices (McKay 1997). This table only says which coarse deck invariants separate the small census.
deck_invariants.scope: On the complete graph census for 3 <= n <= 6, the excess of graphs over classes of the deck-certified degree sequence, and over degree sequence plus triangle count.
deck_invariants.title: Deck invariants that separate the census

frankl_orbits.frontier: Exhaustive verification for ground sets of size at most 4 is already in this repository. The orbit count is the symmetry reduction the n = 5 enumeration still needs. Not a theorem.
frankl_orbits.scope: Every nontrivial union-closed family on a ground set of size at most 4 satisfies Frankl's abundance bound, and the number of families up to relabelling is the recorded orbit count.
frankl_orbits.title: Orbits of union-closed families under ground-set permutation

goldbach_growth.frontier: Known through 4*10^18 (Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi, 2014). This table only locates the record least primes inside a tiny initial segment.
goldbach_growth.scope: For every even n with 4 <= n <= 20000, the least prime p such that n-p is prime, and the pairs (n, p) where that least prime sets a new record.
goldbach_growth.title: Running-maximum least Goldbach prime

poset_balance.frontier: The conjecture is verified through 11 elements (Peczarski) and proved for width 2 (Linial 1984). The table names the extremal posets inside this census.
poset_balance.scope: Every non-chain poset on at most 6 elements has best balance at least 1/3, and the width-height profile of those whose best balance is exactly 1/3 is the recorded multiset.
poset_balance.title: Posets attaining balance exactly 1/3

straus_patterns.frontier: Classical identities leave n = 1 (mod 24) uncovered. The table clusters one explicit solution per such prime in a finite range. It is not an identity and not a proof.
straus_patterns.scope: Every prime n <= 8000 with n = 1 (mod 24) has an explicit positive solution of 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z, grouped by the residue 4x - n.
straus_patterns.title: Erdos-Straus residue patterns for primes 1 mod 24
